title: International PKU markets
source_note: Market- and policy-facing facts (newborn-screening coverage, who funds formula/medical foods, scaled prevalence, sapropterin/pegvaliase availability, dominant suppliers and advocacy) compiled from ESPKU and national PKU associations, Orphanet and published PKU epidemiology reviews (global prevalence meta-analyses; the 59-country systematic review; the Arab Countries/Turkey/Iran review), WHO and international newborn-screening surveys, and BioMarin/EMA/HAS/NICE/CADTH regulatory and HTA records. Biomedical mechanism deliberately excluded. Patient-population figures scaled from incidence x national birth counts are estimates, not registry counts, and are flagged confidence:estimate; incidence ratios and screening/reimbursement status are sourced where cited.

records.prevalence_note: Incidence ~1:10,000-15,000 live births (~1:12,500 commonly cited); ~16,500 diagnosed patients is an advocacy estimate, not a registry count (estimate)
records.who_pays: Patchwork: private insurance, Medicaid, and state medical-food coverage laws; ~half of states offer no/partial medical-food coverage and ~18 states no adult coverage (access barrier)
records.drug_access: Kuvan: yes (FDA-approved 2007, widely reimbursed, now generic); Palynziq: yes (FDA-approved 2018 adults, expanded to age 12+ in 2026)
records.market_signal: Largest, best-capitalized market with full drug pipeline, but fragmented state/payer medical-food reimbursement is the dominant access barrier

records.market_signal: Universal screening undercut by province-by-province formula and drug reimbursement, a patchwork like the US; advocacy via Canadian PKU and Allied Disorders Association
